source_text:
Fragmenta ex libro iii contra Theodorum Mopsuestenum
ΤΟΥ ΑΥΤΟΥ ΚΥΡΙΛΛΟΥ Ἐκ τοῦ πρὸς τὰ Θεοδώρου ἐπισκόπου
Μοψουεστίας τρίτου λόγου Οὗ ἡ ἁρχή Φορτικοὶ μὲν γὰρ ἴσως οἱ πρὸς
ἡμῶν εἰσι λόγοι. αʹ.
ΑΚΟΥΕ τοίνυν καὶ πρὸς ἡμῶν Σύνες ἄνθρωπε τοῦ μυστηρίου τὸ βάθος, εὐθὺ
τοῦ σκοποῦ τῶν ἱερῶν ἴθι γραμμάτων. ἕτερον μὲν γάρ τι καὶ ἕτερον θεότης τε καὶ
σὰρξ ἤγουν ἀνθρωπότης, τό γε ἧκον εἰς τοὺς ἐνόντας τοῖς ἀμφοῖν ἰδιώμασι λόγους.
ἐπεὶ πῶς γέγονε καθ' ἡμᾶς, καίτοι μεμηνηκὼς ὅπερ ἦν, Θεὸς ὢν ὁ Λόγος;
thought_title: The depth of the mystery: divinity and flesh distinct yet one
orientation: Cyril opens his third book against Theodore by urging him to grasp the depth of the mystery of Christ, insisting that divinity and flesh are distinct in their natural properties yet must be confessed as one Son.
pass_a_gloss: LISTEN then also from us. Understand, man, of the mystery the depth; straight toward the mark of the sacred writings go. One thing [is] for [it is] one thing and another thing divinity and flesh, that is humanity, at least as far as concerns the accounts [that apply] to the properties present in both. Since how did he become as we [are], although having remained what he was, being God, the Word?

choices.why: Direct imperative address to Theodore, keeping the blunt vocative force of the Greek

choices.term: τό γε ἧκον εἰς τοὺς ἐνόντας τοῖς ἀμφοῖν ἰδιώμασι λόγους
choices.english: at least as far as concerns the accounts that apply to the properties present in both
choices.why: Preserves the limiting force of τό γε ἧκον εἰς and the dative of possession
rejected: in respect of the properties belonging to both
as regards the properties inherent in both

choices.why: Perfect participle of μένω, emphasizing the Word's continuing state of being God
Idiomatic rendering of the phrase meaning 'according to our condition' or 'like us'

pass_b_english: Listen, then, to what I also have to say to you. Understand, my friend, the depth of the mystery, and go straight toward the goal of the sacred writings. For divinity and flesh, that is, humanity, are different realities, at least as far as concerns the accounts that apply to the properties present in both. For how, I ask, did he become as we are, when the Word, being God, had remained what he was?

problems.quote: Understand, man, the depth of the mystery
problems.why: Unclear if 'man' addresses Theodore or a generic reader; direct address shifts without signal.
problems.fix: Add note: Cyril addresses Theodore directly throughout.

problems.quote: For divinity and flesh—that is, humanity—are one thing and another
problems.why: 'Are one thing and another' is not natural English; meaning unclear.
problems.fix: Render as 'are distinct from one another' or 'are one and another.'

edits.old: For divinity and flesh—that is, humanity—are one thing and another
edits.new: For divinity and flesh—that is, humanity—are distinct from one another

fixed: The direct address 'man' is already present in the English and reflects the source's direct address to Theodore; no change needed.

problems.quote: Listen, then, to what we also have to say. Understand, my friend, the depth of the mystery
problems.why: Reader cannot tell if 'we' is Cyril alone, Cyril with allies, or a royal/editorial plural; 'my friend' addresses Theodore but tone shifts to adversarial without warning.
problems.fix: Clarify that 'we' is Cyril's authorial plural addressing Theodore.

problems.quote: For divinity and flesh, that is, humanity, are one thing and another
problems.why: 'One thing and another' is awkward gloss; reader may miss that it means 'distinct from each other.'
problems.fix: Render as 'are distinct from one another' or 'are different realities.'

edits.old: Listen, then, to what we also have to say. Understand, my friend, the depth of the mystery
edits.new: Listen, then, to what I also have to say. Understand, my friend, the depth of the mystery

edits.old: For divinity and flesh, that is, humanity, are one thing and another
edits.new: For divinity and flesh, that is, humanity, are different realities

fixed: Changed 'we' to 'I' to clarify Cyril's authorial voice addressing Theodore.
Rendered 'one thing and another' as 'different realities' to convey distinctness without awkward gloss.

problems.quote: Listen, then, to what I also have to say
problems.why: Unclear if Cyril addressing Theodore or quoting himself from larger work
problems.fix: Clarify this is Cyril's direct address to Theodore

problems.quote: For how did he become as we are, when the Word, being God, had remained what he was?
problems.why: Unclear if this is Cyril's own question or a question he attributes to Theodore.
problems.fix: Signal whether this is Cyril's rhetorical question or Theodore's objection.

edits.old: Listen, then, to what I also have to say.
edits.new: Listen, then, to what I also have to say to you.

edits.old: For how did he become as we are, when the Word, being God, had remained what he was?
edits.new: For how, I ask, did he become as we are, when the Word, being God, had remained what he was?

fixed: The first problem is real: the address needed to be made explicitly to Theodore, so I added 'to you'.
The second problem is real: the question needed to be marked as Cyril's own rhetorical question, so I added 'I ask'.

polish.changed: Clarified the direct address to Theodore, rendered the technical term 'mark' as 'goal' for modern readers, and smoothed the awkward phrase 'are one thing and another' into natural English while preserving the distinction between divinity and flesh.

notes.quote: Understand, man, the depth of the mystery
notes.why: Unclear if 'man' addresses Theodore or a generic reader; direct address shifts without signal.
notes.fix: Add note: Cyril addresses Theodore directly throughout.

notes.quote: the mark of the sacred writings
notes.why: 'Mark' (Greek σκοπός) is technical term for interpretive target/center; modern reader misses theological method.
notes.fix: Translate as 'target' or add note on σκοπός.

notes.quote: For divinity and flesh—that is, humanity—are one thing and another
notes.why: 'Are one thing and another' is not natural English; meaning unclear.
notes.fix: Render as 'are distinct from one another' or 'are one and another.'
